equity_bridge.item: Cladding fire-safety provision, post-tax (GBP437.7m at 28 June 2026 x (1 - 25%))
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 provisions note / Analysis JSON. The forward flows are built from adjusted EBITDA before exceptionals, so the remaining remediation obligation is deducted once here. Carried at the discounted provision (unwind GBP3.2m in H1 2026) less the 25% corporation-tax shield recognised as a deferred tax asset; gross deduction would be GBP437.7m (c.3p/share more). Guided cash spend c.GBP100m in FY2026, the balance over roughly four further years. Scotland's Developer Remediation Contract (signed March 2026) is inside the provision; re-estimation risk is to the upside of the liability.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: average base-case revenue growth over the 10-year horizon (FY2026 flat on guidance, FY2027-30 recovery to c.13k completions, fading to 2.5%); historical CAGRs are cycle artefacts (FY2020 COVID base inflates the 5-yr, FY2022 peak base deflates the 3-yr; 10-yr FY2016-25 revenue CAGR is 0.5%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+0.8% 5-yr) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS (-15% 5-yr) and revenue (+6.6% 5-yr): FY2020 is a COVID trough base for revenue, while EPS and owner FCF are depressed by the FY2024-25 cladding provision charges (GBP225.8m net increase FY2025) and the margin cycle. None of the trailing CAGRs is a usable forward rate; the base case is anchored on mid-cycle margins and the FY2026 guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal and interest): FY2022 444.8, FY2023 73.7, FY2024 108.6, FY2025 92.3; FY2020 -328 (COVID land/WIP build), so the 5-yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined on a negative base. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (-40.8%) is below the reported-FCF 3-yr CAGR (-35.8%) because interest income rose with the cash pile while SBC and lease cash were roughly flat; SBC itself is not growing faster than cash flow.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle recovery, not a boom. FY2026 is flat on guidance (10.6-10.8k completions, ASP +1%, 3-4% build-cost inflation, c.9% EBITDA margin). From FY2027 lower mortgage rates and the record outlet count (228) lift completions toward c.13k by FY2030 and the adjusted operating margin recovers to c.13.6% by FY2032 -- well short of the 16-18% target because the Building Safety Levy, Future Homes Standard and affordable contributions are structural. Growth absorbs 40p of land/WIP per GBP1 of revenue. Terminal owner FCF of c.GBP470m in FY2035 is below the FY2018 nominal peak (GBP639m reported), capped at 13x. The remaining cladding provision is deducted post-tax in the bridge; land creditors are treated as operating payables.
scenario_narratives.bull: Investor Day targets delivered: planning reform (NPPF, Planning and Infrastructure Act) and rate cuts restore first-time-buyer demand, completions reach c.14k by FY2029-30 on ASP +2.5%/yr, land at 12.5-13.8% of ASP drives the adjusted operating margin to 16% by FY2032, and the landbank-years cut to 4.5-5.0 releases capital so growth absorbs only 30p per GBP1. Taylor Wimpey re-earns a >15% return on net operating assets and the market pays c.1.5x TNAV again.
scenario_narratives.bear: The prolonged downturn becomes the new normal: sales rates stay near 0.55/outlet/week, FY2027 revenue falls 3%, build-cost inflation and the Building Safety Levy are never recovered in price, so margins trough at 7.5% and settle at c.10%. Growth absorbs 50p per GBP1 of revenue. Cladding costs re-escalate within the provision (not modelled beyond the post-tax deduction), the 4%-of-net-assets distribution is all shareholders see, and the stock is a sub-TNAV value trap earning below its cost of equity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a cyclical homebuilder on mid-cycle owner FCF, not trough or peak earnings. FY2025 adjusted operating margin (10.9%) and H1 2026 (7.7%) are trough prints against a 10-year average of 16.9%; the base case recovers only to 13.6% because the post-Grenfell regulatory cost base is permanent. Three safeguards: (1) cladding remediation is a debt-like obligation deducted once, post-tax, in the bridge; (2) growth is charged for the land and WIP it consumes through a negative working-capital capture; (3) the terminal value is capped at 12-14x FCF rather than letting Gordon growth capitalise a recovery that has not yet happened. The base case lands at roughly 1x tangible net assets per share (117.1p), which is where a UK homebuilder earning a 12% return on equity against a 9.5% cost of equity should trade; bear and bull bracket it at c.0.5x and c.1.5x TNAV, the sector's historical range. The weighted value is a judgement that the cycle turns within the horizon, not a bet on the 16-18% target.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin recovery never arrives: if the adjusted operating margin stays at the FY2023-25 average (12.1%) or below, the base case collapses toward the bear value
Cladding provision re-estimation: each further GBP100m of remediation cost is c.2.1p/share post-tax, and the provision has already been raised twice (FY2025 GBP225.8m, H1 2025 GBP222.2m)
Land creditors treated as operating, not debt: management's own adjusted net debt definition would deduct GBP434.5m (c.12p/share) -- apply that haircut if the landbank stops being replenished
Working-capital absorption on growth is a judgement (40p per GBP1 base); the FY2017-19 actual was 40-80p, so a faster recovery could consume more cash than modelled
Terminal cap of 13x on FY2035 owner FCF assumes a mid-cycle exit; a trough exit (the FY2008 or FY2023 analogue) would be 6-8x
Mortgage affordability and UK fiscal/housing policy (Stamp Duty, equity-loan schemes, Building Safety Levy rate) can move FY2027-28 volumes by +/-15% in either direction

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (regularMarketPrice, GBp) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 73.36-116.93p; the price sits at the bottom of the range
data_sources.financials: TW.L_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2025 annual, H1 2016-H1 2026 half-years, GBP millions, derived from the annual and half-year reports); H1 2026 half-year report for net cash, land creditors, lease liabilities, diluted shares, TNAV and the cladding provision; FY2025 Annual Report for SBC, lease cash, interest received, tax rate
data_sources.qualitative: TW.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): Building Safety Act context, FY2026 guidance (H1 2026 results 31 July 2026), October 2025 Investor Day medium-term targets, July 2026 trading update and distribution-policy cut

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment charge' 8.9 (TW.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:9714); no net-share-settlement tax line disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 across history), so the cash-flow add-back is the combined figure
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of own shares GBP3.3m; H1 2026 GBP52.7m completed (H1 2026 cash flow note 12); a further GBP42m buyback announced 31 July 2026 is post-balance-date and not in the share count. Buybacks are value-neutral here (SBC is expensed; count held flat).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP (millions); LSE quote in pence (GBp). fx_rate 100 = pence per pound, a fixed unit conversion with no FX risk and no parity check required. Per-share values are computed in GBP and multiplied by 100 to pence.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,521.1m ordinary shares in issue at 28 June 2026 (H1 2026 TNAV note) plus 6.2m dilutive share awards (diluted 3,527.6m less basic 3,521.4m weighted average, H1 2026 note 8) = 3,527.3m fully diluted. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The GBP42m buyback announced July 2026 (~55m shares at ~75p) is not reflected; it is value-neutral under the flat-count convention.
inputs.net_cash_basis: H1 2026 balance sheet, 28 June 2026: cash GBP254.8m less borrowings GBP86.2m = net cash GBP168.6m (company-defined net cash, H1 2026 APM note). Lease liabilities (GBP39.8m) EXCLUDED under lease treatment (B). Land creditors (GBP434.5m) treated as operating working capital, not debt -- see notes. Management guides c.GBP250m year-end FY2026 net cash after c.GBP100m cladding cash spend.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-denominated flows discounted at a GBP-built rate: 10-year gilt c.4.5% + 5.0% UK ERP x beta 1.0 = 9.5% cost of equity; the group is net cash with GBP86m of borrowings against GBP4.1bn of equity so WACC = cost of equity. Cyclicality is charged ONCE -- in the scenario paths and their weights -- so no ad-hoc premium is stacked and all three scenarios use the same 9.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: FY2025 lease principal GBP11.6m (financing) + lease interest GBP1.6m (operating) = GBP13.2m, 0.34% of revenue, charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (GBP39.8m at H1 2026) excluded from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (owned PPE depreciation c.0.4% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; all profit attributable to equity holders. Joint-venture share of profit (c.GBP4m FY2026 guidance) is off-balance-sheet revenue and is ignored -- immaterial (<1% of value).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, with the cyclical/non-US adaptations (GBP WACC, single lease treatment, excluded-income matching, risk charged once). Taylor Wimpey is a going-concern operating homebuilder with ten years of reported FCF (GBP500-640m at the FY2016-19 peak, GBP120-160m in the FY2023-25 trough), so the owner-FCF engine applies with a MID-CYCLE framing: FY0 (FY2025) is a trough year (adjusted operating margin 10.9%, H1 2026 7.7%, vs a 10-year average of 16.9%) and the driver paths recover toward a mid-cycle margin deliberately set BELOW management's 16-18% Investor Day target to reflect the permanently higher regulatory cost base (Building Safety Levy from Oct 2026, Future Homes Standard, affordable-housing contributions). The routing table's 'inventory-heavy developer -> blended NTA/P-E' row was considered: TNAV per share is 117.1p at H1 2026 and is used as a cross-check (the base IV lands at c.1x TNAV, consistent with a 12% mid-cycle return on equity against a 9.5% cost of equity), but the DCF is the primary model because the business recycles its landbank continuously rather than liquidating it. OWNER FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 126.5 (OCF 133.2 - capex 6.7) - SBC 8.9 - interest income 12.1 - lease cash 13.2 = 92.3. Interest income is stripped because net cash (168.6) exceeds the FCF base; the matching asset (cash) is in the bridge. FY2025 reported FCF also absorbed cladding remediation cash and the GBP18m CMA contribution, both exceptional and outside adjusted EBITDA -- the forward flows are built from ADJUSTED EBITDA (before exceptionals), so the remaining cladding obligation is deducted once, in the equity bridge, as the post-tax provision. LAND CREDITORS (GBP434.5m at H1 2026, GBP522.5m at FY2025) are excluded from the stored TotalDebt and are NOT added to net debt here: they are deferred land payments replenished as new land is bought on deferred terms, i.e. a permanent operating payable like trade creditors, and their settlement is captured through the negative working-capital capture on revenue growth. Management's own 'adjusted net debt' (net cash less land creditors) would be GBP-265.9m; treating them as debt would cut every scenario by c.12p/share, and the reader can apply that haircut from this note. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (growth consumes land and WIP); FY2017-19 showed GBP96-196m of inventory build per year against GBP117-289m of revenue growth (40-80% capture), moderated here to 40% in the base because management plans to grow completions toward 14k while cutting landbank years from 7.2 to 4.5-5.0 (growth largely from the strategic pipeline without net land investment). TAX: 29% cash rate = 25% UK corporation tax + 4% Residential Property Developer Tax (FY2025 note, 'Tax at the UK corporation tax rate of 29.0%'); the FY2025 cash tax paid of GBP50m was depressed by cladding deductions and is not a repeatable base. SBC is small (0.23% of revenue) but kept explicit; house and street differ only marginally. PRICE: the quote is a regular LSE close, not after-hours.
inputs.cyclical_context: 10-year adjusted operating margin history FY2016-FY2025: 20.8, 21.0, 21.4, 19.4, 10.5 (COVID), 19.2, 20.5, 13.3, 12.2, 10.9; H1 2026 7.7%. Completions FY2019 peak 15,719; FY2025 10,735 (10,614 ex-JV); FY2026 guided 10,600-10,800; medium-term target c.14,000. Net private sales rate 0.55/outlet/week in the four weeks to 26 July 2026 vs 0.59 prior year, the fifth consecutive period of decline; July 2026 distribution policy cut from 7.5% to 4% of net assets.

bear.rationale: The downturn stays prolonged: FY2026 completions at the bottom of guidance with underlying prices 2% below prior year, FY2027 revenue -3% as the 0.55 sales rate flows through to completions, margins trough at 7.5% as 3-4% build-cost inflation and the Building Safety Levy are not recovered in price, and the mid-cycle margin settles at c.10% adjusted operating margin -- the FY2023-25 trough becomes the new normal. Land absorption at 50p per GBP1 of growth (no landbank-years benefit). Cap 12x.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +0.5%: completions guided 10,600-10,800 vs 10,614 FY2025, blended UK ASP +1%, Spain completions falling. FY2027-30: recovery as mortgage rates ease and outlets (228 at H1 2026, +9% YoY) convert to completions -- reaches c.13k UK completions by FY2030 at c.2%/yr ASP growth, short of the 14k medium-term target. Fades to 2.5% nominal by FY2033.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA margin (adjusted operating profit + owned-PPE D&A, before exceptionals). FY2026 9.0% (H1 2026 7.7% adjusted operating margin, H2 seasonally stronger; build cost inflation 3-4% vs ASP +1% caps the recovery). Ramps to 14.0% by FY2032 = 13.6% adjusted operating margin, between the FY2023-25 average (12.1%) and the 10-year average (16.9%), and deliberately below the 16-18% Investor Day target because the Building Safety Levy, Future Homes Standard and affordable-housing contributions are a permanent cost-base step-up.
base.wc_rationale: Negative capture: each GBP1 of revenue growth absorbs 40p of land and WIP. FY2017-19 actual absorption was 40-80% of revenue growth at a 7-year landbank; moderated because the landbank-years target (4.5-5.0) means volume growth is funded largely from the existing strategic pipeline.
base.terminal_rationale: Terminal growth 2.0% (UK nominal GDP trend, housing volumes flat long-run); cap 13x terminal owner FCF, within the 12-15x cyclical band -- Gordon at 9.5%/2.0% would be 13.6x so the cap binds marginally.

bull.rationale: Investor Day targets delivered: c.14k completions by FY2029-30 with a 2.5%/yr ASP tailwind (revenue c.GBP5.2bn by FY2030), adjusted operating margin reaching the bottom of the 16-18% range by FY2032, and the landbank-years reduction cutting growth-driven working-capital absorption to 30p per GBP1 of revenue. Cap 14x reflects a business that has re-earned a mid-teens return on net operating assets.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: five consecutive periods of declining sales rates, a FY2026 completions guidance cut, a July 2026 distribution-policy cut from 7.5% to 4% of net assets, build-cost inflation running 2-3pp ahead of pricing, and an open-ended cladding liability that has re-escalated twice. Bull cut to 20% because it requires three independent things -- demand recovery, delivery of the 16-18% margin target against a rising regulatory cost base, and the landbank-years reduction -- to all come through. Base 50%: mid-cycle recovery to a margin below target.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
